clue.text: Frenzy in shooting gallery when Nationalist released

indicators.note: something released is let go, so that letter is set free from the word and leaves it

blocks.note: a rifle range is a place for target shooting
N is the standard abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper at a fairground shooting stall once a nationalist is freed.
explanation.walkthrough: RANGE loses its N to leave RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is violent uncontrolled anger, the same wild state as a frenzy.

clue.text: I love to run around in circle

indicators.note: running around suggests moving every which way, so the letters are scattered and reset

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A jogger declares a fondness for doing laps of a circular track.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolution is one complete turn about a centre, i.e. a full circuit or circle.

clue.text: Criticised, as bit of toast found in butter

indicators.note: a thing found in another sits inside it, so one piece lies within the other

blocks.note: a goat butts with its head, so it is a butter in the crossword sense
the first letter of toast

explanation.surface: Someone complains about crumbs of toast left in the butter dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is the spread in the surface but an animal that butts in the wordplay: GO(T)AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone is an idiom meaning to nag or criticise them persistently.

clue.text: Asthmatic Republican vandalised Dutch city

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so these letters are broken and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A wheezy Republican goes on a destructive spree in a Netherlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: Maastricht is a city in the southern Netherlands, famous for the EU treaty signed there.

clue.text: Fate of American soldiers with pressure rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means moving upward, so the pressure letter climbs one place past its neighbour

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
troops are soldiers; this word already holds the pressure letter
P is the symbol for pressure, the letter that moves

explanation.surface: A news report on what became of US troops when pressure on them mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: A + TROOPS, then the P rises above the O beside it: TROOPS becomes TROPOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the one who cuts the thread of life.

clue.text: That woman has managed to inhale drug in hookah

indicators.note: breathing in draws something inside, so one piece is taken within the other
managed here means handled or worked over, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the pronoun for that woman
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman manages to breathe in some substance while smoking a water pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug goes in first and only then is the little word shuffled, so the container and anagram apply in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheesha is the Middle Eastern water pipe also called a hookah or hubble-bubble.

clue.text: Clever to start late, correct?

indicators.note: late can mean dead, so the opening letter has died and is gone

blocks.note: a bright pupil is a clever one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being late to begin is a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy, but here means dead: BRIGHT loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are synonyms for being accurate or true.

clue.text: French footballer, mostly with no difficulty, picked up foreign language

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of that name is dropped
picked up as in caught by ear, so we want something that sounds like the words

blocks.note: Eric Cantona, French striker famous at Manchester United
ease is freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: A French footballer learns a foreign tongue with very little trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: CANTON(a) plus EASE, said aloud, gives the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is the Chinese language spoken in Hong Kong and Guangdong.

clue.text: Spelling of 'doughnuts'?

definitions.note: a first name: the answer is the first name of Spelling

blocks.note: first meaning: ... Spelling, the American actress
second meaning: the plural of torus, the mathematical ring shape

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking how to spell a word; Spelling is in fact a surname, and doughnuts are the geometric ring shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Tori Spelling is the Beverly Hills 90210 actress, and tori is the plural of torus, a ring-shaped surface.

clue.text: Conclude I love rector's pants to a greater degree

blocks.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: Someone decides they love the vicar's trousers more than anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, so more pants means worse; it is not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means of lower quality, i.e. worse, which is being more rubbish than something else.

clue.text: Barrel is enormous, not small

indicators.note: not marks something that must be left out of the word

blocks.note: vast means enormous
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A boast that a cask is huge rather than little.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tank or tub for liquids, much like a barrel.

clue.text: Eagles' running back eats treat

indicators.note: something that eats a thing holds it inside, so the phrase is holding the answer within itself
going back means travelling the other way, so the concealed letters read from right to left

blocks.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: An American football player for the Philadelphia Eagles enjoys a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe and the sporting picture hide the join across the two words. A running back is the American football ball carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to treat or care for them while they are ill.

clue.text: Individual with no hope shot Norse queen

blocks.note: a shot at something is a go
N is the abbreviation for Norse
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A doomed person fires on a Viking queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a past tense of shooting but is a noun meaning an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is informal for someone beyond saving, a person who is finished.

clue.text: French article and English translation for metalworker

blocks.note: la is the French feminine definite article
the is what that French article means in English

explanation.surface: A French grammar point and its English rendering are offered to someone who works metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part translates the first: 'the' in French is la.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that turns and shapes metal, so it does metalworking itself.

clue.text: Job? No, it is work to be rebuffed

indicators.note: something rebuffed is pushed back, so the words run in the other direction

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an offer of employment, saying the work will be refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A position is a post in employment, the same as a job.

clue.text: Promising individual shot unarmed cop

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so those letters are broken up

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A rising star gunned down a policeman without a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-and-comer is someone likely to succeed soon, a rising talent.

clue.text: Plans to do something to stop twitches

indicators.note: a stopper sits in a gap, so one piece is plugged inside the other

blocks.note: tics are involuntary twitches
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: Schemes for taking action to cure nervous spasms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' reads as preventing, but here means plugging the gap inside the twitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are the plans or methods used to achieve a goal.

clue.text: Function of powerful whip cracking

indicators.note: cracking something open breaks into it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cogent argument is a powerful one
to tan someone's hide is to beat or whip them

explanation.surface: What a forceful whip crack does.
explanation.walkthrough: TAN breaks into COGENT: CO(TAN)GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cotangent is a trigonometric function, the reciprocal of the tangent.

clue.text: Refuse pile of money, economical when Conservatives ditched

indicators.note: things ditched are thrown away, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: cash is money
cheap means economical
C abbreviates Conservative, and two are wanted

explanation.surface: A heap of money saved once the Tories were thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: One C leaves the front of CASH and one the front of CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash heap is a dump for ashes and rubbish, a refuse pile.

clue.text: Eat and throw up, creating trouble

indicators.note: up as in messed up or disturbed, so those letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating and then vomiting leads to difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw up' is not the indicator phrase it seems; only 'up' signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in hot water is an idiom for being in trouble or disgrace.

clue.text: Corrupt monster having friendly relations

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so those letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishonest ogre is getting on well with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on terms with someone is an idiom for being on friendly or speaking terms.

clue.text: Bird box with chain

blocks.note: to spar is to box
a chain of things in a line is a row

explanation.surface: A birdcage fitted with a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container noun, but it is the verb to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird.

clue.text: In joint possession of punt, we went naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so only the inside of the word stays

blocks.note: a punt is a wager, a bet
taken as written
the inner letters of went

explanation.surface: Two people went skinny-dipping from a shared flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests the boat; here it is a gamble. A punt is a flat boat poled along rivers in Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shared between two people is held jointly by them, as in 'between us we own it'.

clue.text: Roger, in bed, didn't cause problems

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
roger and have are both slang for having sex with someone

explanation.surface: A man called Roger lay in bed and gave no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a name, but is the British slang verb for sex: BE(HAVE)D.
explanation.definitionFit: To have behaved is to have acted properly, avoiding causing any trouble.

clue.text: Redneck regularly gets swimmer to overstep the mark

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin often catches a fish, then goes too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is the setter's way of saying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude beyond proper limits, so it means to overstep the mark.

clue.text: Old-fashioned baggage attendant quietly declined to go back

indicators.note: that letter refuses to come along, so it is left out
back means the rest is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a porter carries luggage
P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A dated hotel porter softly refuses to return.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER drops P to leave ORTER, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style imitating or reviving the past, so it is deliberately dated.

clue.text: Reportedly put wine in for a particular purpose

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to put in is to add; hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Someone apparently tipped wine into a dish for a specific reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is the British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'to this', meaning arranged for one specific purpose only.

clue.text: Carnivore in hotel with desire to get ham, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter is wanted

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a yen is a longing or desire
the centre letter of ham

explanation.surface: A meat-eater in a hotel craves a bit of ham.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a flesh-eating African mammal, a scavenger and predator.

clue.text: Soldier captures island in ocean

indicators.note: capturing something takes it prisoner, so it is held inside

blocks.note: a man is a private soldier
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A soldier seizes an island out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary term for the high seas, the open ocean.

clue.text: Warning! Beer at room temperature, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the initial letters are taken

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
the opening letters of room and temperature

explanation.surface: A caution that the beer is being served unchilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Ale is served at cellar temperature in Britain, which gives the surface its joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal or notice warning of danger.

clue.text: Critical examination in audition for theatrical performance

indicators.note: audition is literally hearing, so the word is taken by sound

blocks.note: a review is a critical examination

explanation.surface: Someone is closely scrutinised while trying out for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a stage tryout, which suits the definition, but it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light stage entertainment of songs, sketches and dances.

clue.text: Half of Elon Musk's head is wood

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts is kept
a head is the top, so the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first two of the four letters
the first letter of Musk

explanation.surface: A jibe that the billionaire's brain is partly made of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber from the elm tree.

clue.text: I waited on northern criminal throughout the land

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so those letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N abbreviates northern

explanation.surface: A waiter served a northern villain, across the whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide means extending across a whole country, everywhere in the land.

clue.text: Couple one over par? Just the opposite

indicators.note: over can mean covering, putting one thing on top of and around another
this flips which piece covers which, so the score now wraps the numeral rather than the other way round

blocks.note: par is the standard score in golf
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A golf question about a couple who scored a bogey, one more than par.
explanation.walkthrough: As written, the numeral would wrap the score; 'Just the opposite' swaps the roles so the golf score goes around the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two people or things together, a couple.
